sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: A DYNAMIC LARGE-SCALE PATTERN WILL EXIST OVER THE CENTRAL CONUS ON DAY 1 AS AN INTENSE MID/UPPER-LEVEL LOW SHIFTS NEWD FROM THE CENTRAL HIGH PLAINS INTO SD/NEB. IN THE LOW LEVELS...STRONG CYCLOGENESIS IS EXPECTED TO BE UNDERWAY ACROSS NERN CO AT 12Z TODAY. THIS LOW SHOULD UNDERGO SOME DEEPENING THIS MORNING AS IT TRACKS NEWD INTO CENTRAL NEB...AND THEN BEGIN TO FILL FROM LATE THIS AFTERNOON INTO TONIGHT. THE LOW IS PROGGED TO REACH SERN/ERN SD BY 12Z TUESDAY. A TRAILING COLD FRONT WILL MOVE ENEWD ACROSS NEB/NRN KS DURING THE FIRST HALF OF THE PERIOD. MEANWHILE...A DRY LINE WILL MIX EWD REACHING CENTRAL KS TO WRN OK BY EARLY-MID AFTERNOON. sections.text: FORCING FOR ASCENT WILL SPREAD NEWD ACROSS THE CENTRAL PLAINS ATTENDANT TO A LEAD MID LEVEL IMPULSE ACCOMPANYING THE MID/UPPER LEVEL LOW/TROUGH. MODELS SUGGEST INITIAL SURFACE BASED STORMS SHOULD DEVELOP BY EARLY AFTERNOON ACROSS CENTRAL/SRN NEB AND ADJACENT NRN KS ALONG TRACK OF THE SURFACE LOW. THIS ACTIVITY SHOULD THEN SPREAD ENEWD INTO THE MID MO RIVER VALLEY AS DEEP LAYER ASCENT WEAKENS THE CAP OVER THIS REGION AND THE COLD FRONT PROGRESSES ENEWD OVERTAKING THE PRE-FRONTAL TROUGH/DRY LINE. HAIL/DAMAGING WINDS WILL BE THE PRIMARY SEVERE WEATHER THREATS ACROSS THIS REGION. HOWEVER...THE SETUP WILL BE FAVORABLE FOR LOW-TOPPED SUPERCELL DEVELOPMENT ALONG TRACK OF SURFACE LOW WHERE ISOLATED TORNADOES ARE POSSIBLE. sections.text: A CAP EXTENDING FROM CENTRAL/SRN KS SWD THROUGH THE RED RIVER VALLEY IS EXPECTED TO LIMIT TSTM DEVELOPMENT UNTIL MID-LATE AFTERNOON. sections.text: SUBSTANTIAL /90-150 M/ HEIGHT FALLS WILL PROGRESS STEADILY ENE ACROSS KS/NEB AND SRN SD TODAY AS CO UPR LOW CONTINUES NEWD. THE HEIGHT FALLS WILL BE ACCOMPANIED BY ASCENT IN EXIT REGION OF ASSOCIATED UPR JET STREAK...AND WITH LOW LVL UPLIFT ALONG PACIFIC COLD FRONT. DEEP SHEAR WILL BE STRONG /40-50 KTS/ THROUGHOUT REGION...ALTHOUGH WITH A SUBSTANTIAL COMPONENT ORIENTED PARALLEL TO FRONT IN SD AND NEB. sections.text: THE EXIT REGION OF THE STRONG POLAR JET STREAK IS ALREADY SHIFTING NORTHEASTWARD ACROSS THE NORTH CENTRAL PLAINS...WITH AN INITIAL IMPULSE PIVOTING AROUND THE EASTERN PERIPHERY OF A CLOSED MID-LEVEL CIRCULATION OVER WEST CENTRAL NEBRASKA. sections.title: SYNOPSIS
sections.text: LATEST MODELS/OBSERVATIONAL DATA CONTINUE TO SUPPORT EXPECTED EVOLUTION OF ONGOING SEVERE WEATHER THREAT ACROSS A LARGE PART OF THE PLAINS ENEWD INTO LOWER MO VALLEY AND UPPER MIDWEST. AREAS FROM IA SWWD THROUGH WRN MO/ERN KS TO OK ARE EXPECTED TO HAVE THE GREATEST SEVERE WEATHER THREAT THROUGH THE EVENING/OVERNIGHT PERIOD. EARLY EVENING SURFACE ANALYSIS INDICATED TWO AREAS OF LOW PRESSURE...1. OVER CENTRAL NEB AND 2. OVER CENTRAL SD. MODELS SUGGEST THE LOWS SHOULD CONSOLIDATE ACROSS ERN SD BY 12Z TUESDAY AS THE DEEP TROPOSPHERIC LOW CENTERS BECOME MORE VERTICALLY STACKED ACROSS SD LATE IN THE FORECAST PERIOD. COLD FRONT ARCED SEWD THROUGH CENTRAL NEB AND THEN SSWWD THROUGH CENTRAL TO SWRN KS. THE NEB PORTION OF THIS FRONT WILL CONTINUE TO SURGE ENEWD THROUGH ERN NEB/SERN SD THIS EVENING AND SHOULD REACH CENTRAL MN TO CENTRAL IA BY 12Z TUESDAY. MEANWHILE...THE KS PORTION OF THE COLD FRONT WILL MOVE ESEWD THROUGH KS AND ALSO INTO OK...MERGING WITH AND OVERTAKING A DRY LINE. AT 00Z...THE DRY LINE EXTENDED SWD FROM A TRIPLE POINT IN CENTRAL KS THROUGH WRN OK WHERE IT HAD BECOME QUASI-STATIONARY INTO FAR SWRN OK.

sections.title: ERN KS/OK/NW-N TX INTO WRN MO/SRN IA
sections.text: SHORT WAVE TROUGH/VORTICITY LOBE LOCATED OVER ERN NEB INTO ERN KS WILL CONTINUE TO TRACK NEWD ACROSS THE LOWER MO RIVER VALLEY THIS EVENING REACHING THE UPPER MS VALLEY LATE IN THE DAY 1 PERIOD. FORCING FOR ASCENT WITH THIS FEATURE COMBINED WITH ADDITIONAL ASCENT ATTENDANT TO A STRONG MID LEVEL JET /90 KT/ CURRENTLY TRANSLATING INTO CENTRAL OK WILL SUPPORT ONGOING AND ADDITIONAL TSTM DEVELOPMENT FROM OK NEWD THROUGH ERN KS...REACHING WRN-NRN MO/SRN-CENTRAL IA. GRADUAL HEIGHT FALLS ARE ALSO EXPECTED ACROSS THE SRN PLAINS OVERNIGHT WITH THE APPROACH OF AN UPSTREAM SHORT WAVE TROUGH... CURRENTLY MOVING THROUGH THE FOUR CORNERS REGION. THIS WILL SUPPORT A STRENGTHENING SSWLY LLJ FROM CENTRAL TX INTO THE LOWER MO VALLEY TONIGHT...MAINTAINING A NARROW CORRIDOR OF MOISTURE RETURN/ZONE OF INSTABILITY FOR ADDITIONAL STRONG TO SEVERE STORMS.
